candidates.source_title: Fire festival returns ahead of Christmas lights switch-on - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Final preparations are under way for nest week’s Ignite Fire Festival and Christmas lights switch-on. Ignite Fire Festival, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK, will be transforming the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall, including the new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes from Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22. This free night-time event will open from 5pm to 8pm, delivering a magical trail of fire, lights and sound. Organiser Rochdale Development Agency says this year will be the best yet with new dazzling trails and attractions. Immersive night-time trail BODY will take centre stage, bringing visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite will be its north-west premiere, after having previously travelled over the globe, from Ireland to Canada. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on a dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism — the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. There will also be a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall with pyrotechnics, transforming it into a place of beauty. Back again for 2026 is Drum Machine — the 20-strong drumming collective who will be bringing their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival. Also returning are Fireflies as part of the Culture Co-op programme with Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts.

candidates.source_title: Ollie Pearce goal secures maximum points for York at Rochdale - Wilts and Gloucestershire Standard
candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City tasted victory on the ground where they secured promotion from the National League last season as Ollie Pearce’s goal gave them a 1-0 win at the Crown Oil Arena. Rochdale started brightly, with Dajaune Brown’s header cleared off the line by Harry Boyes six minutes in. On the stroke of half-time, Glenn Middleton was presented with a one-on-one opportunity only for York goalkeeper Alfie McNally to read his attempted dink finish and collect the ball comfortably. In between, the Minstermen had the better of the opening 45 minutes as Hiram Boateng’s effort deflected narrowly wide and Alex Hunt’s rising drive from 20 yards thumped an upright. McNally had to scramble across his goalline to save Brown’s 50th-minute header, and within five minutes the visitors had the lead when Pearce pounced and diverted the ball beyond Sam Waller and into the net. Aden Flint saw an 80th-minute header cleared off the line as Rochdale threatened an equaliser before McNally denied Ian Henderson and Ryan East as York resisted late home pressure.

On the stroke of half-time, Glenn Middleton was presented with a one-on-one opportunity only for York goalkeeper Alfie McNally to read his attempted dink finish and collect the ball comfortably. In between, the Minstermen had the better of the opening 45 minutes as Hiram Boateng’s effort deflected narrowly wide and Alex Hunt’s rising drive from 20 yards thumped an upright. McNally had to scramble across his goalline to save Brown’s 50th-minute header, and within five minutes the visitors had the lead when Pearce pounced and diverted the ball beyond Sam Waller and into the net. Aden Flint saw an 80th-minute header cleared off the line as Rochdale threatened an equaliser before McNally denied Ian Henderson and Ryan East as York resisted late home pressure.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale 0-1 York: City clinch first away win of the season to defeat old foes - The York Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: York City ended their long wait for a first away win of the season as a single goal separated the Minstermen and old title foes Rochdale. York’s last league win away from the LNER Community Stadium came at Tamworth in April, almost seven months ago. Returning to the stadium where City lifted the National League title 203 days ago, it was a reunion that Scott Lindsey’s side took in their stride to clinch a sixth win of their League Two campaign. Josh Stones might have been the hero in Rochdale last April, but it was strike partner Ollie Pearce that took the plaudits on Saturday as he bagged the only goal. Having come close in the first-half, striking the post, he got his reward in the second when flicking Ollie Banks’ low cross past Sam Waller. Rochdale had chances of their own, and having controlled the final 20 minutes, City’s defensive qualities were put to the test. Ryan Fallowfield had to make two goalline clearances, one in the first-half and another in the second, while Alfie McNally thwarted Ian Henderson in the final five minutes. But the Minstermen held on – with head coach Lindsey ending a barren run on the road that had been lingering over his career with York to date.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A man who played a significant role in an organised crime group which supplied class A drugs across Rochdale has been jailed for 10 years and six months. An investigation into Haider Ali was launched following information received that a drug deal had taken place from a car parked in Baron Street, in Rochdale town centre, just before midnight on January 4, 2025. Officers began to follow the vehicle and when it came to a stop at a local petrol station, officers immediately executed a reinforced stop to prevent it from making off. Ali, who was travelling as a passenger, exited the vehicle and began to speedily walk away before officers detained him. Following searches, Ali was found to be in possession of more than £1,000 in cash, and two mobile phones, all of which were seized. Ali was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of class A drugs and taken to custody where further searches recovered two bundles of several wraps of a brown and a white substance. Tests later confirmed these substances to be heroin and cocaine. A pre-paid mobile phone seized from Ali was confirmed to be the Adam drug line. Following this, investigators also uncovered that Ali was not only dealing drugs at street level, but he was also managing other street dealers. Evidence suggested that Ali had progressed from being a street dealer in 2014 to holding a significant role within the Adam OCG in 2024 into 2025, managing street dealers and the dedicated dealer phone, and directing those below him on where there next deal is.

candidates.source_title: Warning to think twice about buying e-bikes and e-scooters this Christmas - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A hard-hitting warning has been issued about the dangers of illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas approaches. Greater Manchester Police and its partners are urging families to think carefully before buying off-road bikes, illegal e-bikes and e-scooters as Christmas gifts, warning that vehicles used unlawfully could be seized and destroyed — or lead to tragedy. The warning comes as part of Operation Hurricane, GMP’s coordinated crackdown on the anti-social and dangerous use of off-road bikes, e-bikes and quad bikes across Greater Manchester. One family which knows the devastating consequences they can cause is that of Jacob Calland, who died after being hit by a car while he was a passenger on an e-scooter when it went through a red light in Wythenshawe in March this year. He died from his injuries eight days later. Jacob’s mother, Carly Calland, said: “No words will ever be able to describe the pain caused by Jacob’s death. My heart has been smashed into a thousand pieces and there is nothing that can be done to fix it. My life is a living nightmare. “I climbed into the hospital bed to cuddle him and I fell asleep holding him. When I woke up, it was time to turn off the machines. I told Jacob I loved him just before he passed away. My baby boy was gone forever. “He won’t sit his GCSEs, he won’t have his sweet sixteen birthday party, he won’t go to his school prom. He won’t be able to follow his dreams. He won’t get married and won’t have children. His life ended the moment that collision happened.” The e-scooter rider, who was 14 at the time, received an 18-month youth referral order and a five-year driving ban after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving, causing death by driving unlicensed, and causing death by driving uninsured.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands of people across the borough gathered to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country, with commemorations taking place on Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day on Wednesday. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for parades and services in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, For the Fallen: “They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. candidates.source_title: Rochdale AFC v York City: Minstermen chase fresh Spotland milestone with 'caged lion' desperate to feature - Yorkshire Post
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Some 204 days will have elapsed between the Minstermen's two visits there in 2026. Saturday's appointment will create nothing like the incredulous theatre of events on April 25, but the hope among the York contingent is that it produces another milestone moment, nevertheless. Back in late spring, York ended their decade-long absence from the Football League in the most scarcely-believable stoppage-time finale ever. On this occasion, the wait for the Minstermen revolves around securing their maiden away victory as an EFL club once again. Their last win on the road as a league club was back in September 2015. Scott Lindsey wasn't present in Lancashire, last time out, but he stressed that those astonishing scenes will form part of his pre-match preparations, as the majority of York players are still at the club. The York chief said: "I think it's important that the players feel that environment when they turn up at the stadium again. I can't comment on that because I obviously wasn't here then. "But all that they will remember are good memories from that stadium. And I think that is important. So we'll definitely be leaning on that. "I think it's important that we do mention it. "But it's for the players to remember those memories. It can only be a good thing that the last time they were there, what happened." The hero last time out was Josh Stones, whose 103rd-minute goal sparked ecstatic scenes among York's 1,500-following and 4,000-odd watching the beam-back at the LNER Community Stadium. Stones had done it tough since and is being integrated back into the first-team following a lumbar glute injury. Suffice to say, he is desperate to be involved at Dale. Lindsey added: "It's like caging a lion, isn't it? He'll be coming out of the traps ready to go again. "I think he showed some frustration in the fact that he didn't play in the Bradford game. He wanted to play, which is great. I want players who want to play, which is fantastic. "But we have to be really mindful of his load, bearing in mind he's been out for so long. And hopefully we get a fresher Josh Stones who can come on the pitch on Saturday and make a real impact. "And the more we do that, the closer we're getting to him to be a starter for us."

Alam Investments has been granted planning permission by Rochdale Council to turn the former office building at St James Place, 168 Yorkshire Street, in Rochdale town centre, into 21 self-contained apartments. The redevelopment of the three-storey building will include a mix of 17 one-bedroom flats and four two-bedroom flats. Planning documents submitted with the application state: “The building has been vacant for approximately eight years and is in need of investment and reuse. “The proposed scheme will bring the property back into productive use, provide much-needed housing in a sustainable location, and contribute positively to the vitality and regeneration of Rochdale town centre. “The property lies adjacent to notable heritage assets, including St Mary’s Ukrainian Catholic Church (Grade II listed), and is surrounded by a mix of commercial and residential uses. “In terms of heritage value, the building itself is of limited architectural and historic significance, lacking distinctive features of merit. Its primary contribution to the conservation area arises from its form, scale, and materiality, which ensure a degree of consistency within the surrounding townscape. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice has reported a series of thefts and attempted break-ins at its charity shops this week, with replacement windows at its Emporium expected to cost around £2,000. The hospice said it is working with Greater Manchester Police following incidents at the Emporium and its Oldham Road shop. Thieves initially damaged a window at Springhill Emporium but failed to gain entry, according to the hospice. The premises were targeted again on Tuesday 10 November, when a window was damaged and items were stolen. The hospice estimates that replacing the large windows will cost around £2,000. Its Oldham Road shop was targeted on Thursday night, 12 November, with further damage and losses reported. Springhill said the incidents had devastated staff, who work alongside the local community to raise money to keep hospice services running for Rochdale residents. The hospice is working with Greater Manchester Police and hopes to release further information to help identify those responsible. candidates.source_title: Rochdale IT provider explains how an alternative route can keep business email moving during Microsoft outages
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Microsoft 365 disruption has prompted Rochdale-based award-winning IT provider, No Fuss IT, to encourage businesses to look beyond everyday technical support and consider how they would keep communicating if their usual email service became unavailable. No Fuss IT, whose IT team is led by Finn O’Loughlin, provides email continuity as part of its enhanced approach to proactively supporting businesses, including organisations working towards or maintaining ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 requirements. When email stops working, the consequences can reach much further than an empty inbox. Customer enquiries can go unanswered. Purchase orders can be delayed. Staff can lose access to conversations they need to complete their work, while managers spend time finding out what is happening and deciding what to do next. For businesses affected by the latest Microsoft disruption over the last 24 hours, it raises a practical question. If the main route into your email becomes unavailable, have you got another way through? Think of it like a motorway with an alternative toll road. Most days, the motorway gets everyone where they need to go. It is familiar, convenient and part of the daily routine. But when a major incident closes the carriageway, everyone relying on that same route can find themselves stuck. Knowing that someone is working to reopen it does little to move the queue.

candidates.source_title: Krisnan Inu joins Rochdale Hornets coaching staff - Total Rugby League
candidates.source_body_excerpt: ROCHDALE HORNETS have handed Krisnan Inu a route back into Rugby League. The 39-year-old former New Zealand and Samoa outside back has been appointed assistant to coach Gary Thornton at the Championship club. It follows Ryan Jackson’s departure to become right-hand man to new coach Matt Bramald at Rochdale’s second-tier rivals Keighley Cougars. Inu, who played in both the NRL and Super League, had a brief stint as coach of North Wales Crusaders earlier this year, from late March until the Championship club entered insolvency in May. Before that, he had three seasons on the coaching staff at the old Salford Red Devils, departing when that version of the club, who played in Super League, were liquidated last December. Inu had played for the Red Devils from 2019 to 2021. Over a 16-year career, he also represented Parramatta Eels, New Zealand Warriors, Canterbury Bulldogs, Catalans Dragons, Widnes Vikings, Lezignan and Leigh Centurions (now Leopards), whom he helped win the Championship Grand Final in 2022. He was a member of the squad when New Zealand won the World Cup in 2008, a winger in the 2020 Super League Dream Team and also played rugby union for leading French side Stade Francais. Thornton and Rochdale chairman Andy Mazey see that experience as being highly valuable, and the latter said: “Kris made a name for himself as an important part of Paul Rowley’s successful performance unit at Salford, with a particular emphasis on defence.

The work, to the east of the city centre on the historic Rochdale Canal, is part of the Canal and River Trust's extensive programme of winter repairs covering 2,000 miles of waterway. Earlier this week, a team started fitting new lock gates at Lock 80, near Miles Platting and Victoria Mill. The waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire. The charity, which cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said it would be carrying out hundreds of projects over the next five months to maintain the 'living heritage' of the network that was built in the industrial revolution and still functions today. The new lock gates in Manchester have been handcrafted from oak at the Canal and River Trust's lock gate workshop at Stanley Ferry, Yorkshire, before being craned into place. Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs 1.5 tonnes, with the downstream leaves weighing 2.5 tonnes, and replace gates that were installed around the turn of the millennium, the charity said. Each gate – which has around a 25-year lifespan – is individually made to fit its lock using specialist skills, and once installed, the new gates will help boats continue to navigate the historic stretch of the Rochdale canal for years, the Trust added. candidates.source_title: Lest We Forget: borough falls silent to mark Remembrance Day – Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Thousands gathered across the borough for Remembrance Day services to honour the nation’s war heroes and pay their respects to those who have made sacrifices in defence of the country. Representatives from the Navy, Army and Royal Air Force joined veterans and civic dignitaries for parades and services in Rochdale town centre, Castleton, Heywood, Littleborough, Middleton, Norden, Milnrow and Wardle. Residents gathered as memorials fell silent, with the Last Post played at each service. Each included the immemorial words from Laurence Binyon’s 1914 poem, For the Fallen: “They shall grow not old as we that are left grow old; Age shall not weary them, nor the years condemn; at the going down of the sun and in the morning. We will remember them.” The Armed Forces community, Members of Parliament, Mayor of Rochdale, Council Leader, Councillor Neil Emmott, councillors, faith leaders, local schools and members of the public also laid their own wreaths and gave respects, following moving readings of The Kohima Epitaph: “When you go home, tell them of us and say, for your tomorrow, we gave our today.” Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana, said: “The turnout across the borough was incredible, as people of all ages gathered at memorials in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale to pay their respects. On a poignant and moving Remembrance Day, we honoured the fallen, people of all faiths and no faith, from countries all over the world. It was a day when the whole community fell silent to reflect and remember. “We will forever hold a special place in our hearts, today and always, for those who never came home. Without their selfless dedication and sacrifices, the freedom, liberty and values we take for granted would have been lost. Side by side they fought together, they fell together and secured the peace together. We will always remember them. Lest we forget.” Current or former Armed Forces personnel can register for help or get more information by visiting the Armed forces community page.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has backed calls for the return of an ‘express’ bus service from Heywood to Manchester. The 167 bus service was scrapped 14 years ago, but there have been growing calls for its return. Heywood and Middleton MP Elsie Blundell has pushed for the route to be reinstated since she was elected in 2024. It is understood that the re-imagined 167 bus route would start in Norden, then stop at Bamford, Heywood and Rhodes before heading into the city centre. Mrs Blundell believes the return of the express bus service would be boost the local economy as well as improving transport connectivity between Heywood and the city centre. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Speaking in the House of Commons this week, Mrs Blundell said: “Heywood is the largest town in Greater Manchester without an express bus service into Manchester city centre . “This is something I have pushed for since my election because I know this will transform the lives of the people in my constituency and it will transform the economy there. “What can the government do to support Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) to deliver this service and make sure people in Heywood will have the benefit of buses placed back under public control?” Mrs Blundell believes the express bus can act as a ‘stopgap’ for Heywood residents while they wait for Metrolink trams to be brought into the area. Metrolink coming to Heywood has not been confirmed, but TfGM said previously they are working on a business case for the project. In his response, Prime Minister Andy Burnham criticised the Conservatives opposite him in the chamber for privatising the bus system in the 1980s. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Mr Burnham said: “We all remember when the party opposite me deregulated buses in this country and left people paying high bus fares – and they still are in many parts of the country because they are still deregulated. They pay £3 or £4 for a single journey and many other constituencies. “We will put a £2 cap on these bus fares next year. I can’t speak for the current mayor of Greater Manchester, but I hope she does the same.” Bev Craig, Mr Burnham’s successor as mayor of Greater Manchester, has not publicly declared her support for the return of the 167. However, it is understood she has met with the Heywood and Middleton North MP to discuss her case for the express bus service and Heywood Metrolink. TfGM confirmed they have modelled various options to assess cost, estimated passenger demand/revenue and economic benefits of bringing the 167 into the transport network. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A partnership which links cutting-edge research with innovative businesses has won a top award for recycling carbon fibre waste. The Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) and its project partners have been recognised nationally after winning the Sustainability and Circularity Award at the Composites UK Industry Awards. The award recognises pioneering work that could help transform how carbon fibre waste is reused across the aerospace sector and wider manufacturing industries. Working alongside Cygnet Texkimp, SHD Composites, NCC and Teledyne CML Composites, CEAMS successfully demonstrated a world-first aerospace component manufactured using material containing 100% recycled continuous carbon fibre. The project showed that recycled carbon fibre can achieve levels of stiffness and strength comparable to new material, while using existing industrial manufacturing processes. This creates a realistic route for large-scale adoption across advanced manufacturing sectors. candidates.source_title: Fire festival returns to Rochdale with free entry and Christmas lights switch-on - About Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Final preparations are under way for Ignite Fire Festival taking place at Rochdale Town Hall Square from Friday 20 to Sunday 22 November, leading up to the much anticipated Christmas lights switch-on at the town hall. Ignite Fire Festival, sponsored by car supermarket The Trade Centre UK, will be transforming the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall, including the new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes. This free night-time event will open 5pm – 8pm, delivering a magical trail of fire, lights and sound. Organisers Rochdale Development Agency say this year will be the best yet with new dazzling trails and attractions. Immersive night-time trail, ‘BODY,’ will take centre stage, bringing visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is the most ambitious fire and light installation yet from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists Walk the Plank, and Ignite will be its north-west premiere, after having previously travelled over the globe, from Ireland to Canada. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on a dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism – the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body’s functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. There will also be a Fire Garden providing extra sparkle, illuminating slopes and gardens behind Rochdale Town Hall with pyrotechnics, transforming it into a place of beauty. Back again for 2026 is ‘Drum Machine’ – the 20-strong drumming collective who will be bringing their dance floor grooves and stomping tunes to the festival. Also returning are ‘Fireflies,’ as part of the Culture Co-op programme with Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts, and live fire shows by interactive arts group Travelling Light Circus, alongside residents trained up especially for Ignite, performing fire spinning feats. There will be flame-cooked hot food served each night including Texas BBQ, brisket, mac n cheese, Bratwurst and seasonal drinks. And look out for stalls filled with homemade goods from fantastic local young people – a Teenage Market will also be staged each evening at the event. On the opening night (Friday November 20) from 5.30pm to 7.30pm, you can take part in an Ignite themed ‘Paint the Flame’ pottery painting at Clay & Glaze on Drake Street, a short walk from the festival. You can paint a fire or a dragon-themed mug. The activity is suitable for children and adults. (Charge of £10 per mug applies). Father Christmas and his special guests, including the Mayor of Rochdale, Councillor Faisal Rana , stars from Middleton Arena’s pantomime Cinderella, the borough’s children’s champions and local members of the UK Youth Parliament switch-on the Christmas lights at 5.30pm on Sunday (22 November). The switch-on takes place in front of the town hall after the traditional countdown, whilst Ignite Fire Festival continues until 8pm.

Councillor Neil Emmott, leader of the council, said: “Shaun’s sudden and tragic death has rocked everyone who knew him. He was a man of great integrity, principle and compassion who got on with the job in hand in his own quiet and unassuming way. Shaun was in politics for the right reasons, to improve people’s lives, tackle inequalities and fight for a better world. That was what moved him. On a personal level, I always found Shaun to be a loyal and supportive colleague who cared deeply for the people he represented. He will be deeply missed. My thoughts are with his family and many friends at this time.” Councillor Faisal Rana, Mayor of Rochdale, said: “The death of Shaun is absolutely devastating news, which will leave a considerable void across the community and in the lives of all who knew him. Shaun was a fine colleague, always supportive with a kind word and wise counsel. He was widely trusted, principled and admired across the political divide. A light has gone out across the community at Shaun’s untimely passing. Condolences to his family at this sad time.” If you would like to contribute to About Manchester, contact us here .
